lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Coffee Roasters | Barista | Metro City, USA | Oct 2025 - Present
- Prepared drinks for the morning rush of about 200 orders and kept the bar stocked.
- Opened the café three days a week and handled the daily cash count.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: The same server-rendered search-page achievement is attributed to two entries a year apart.
items.because: The Lumen and Library Room Booking descriptions claim similar load-time and bookings results, making it unclear which entry owns the achievement.

items.says: EDUCATION appears before EXPERIENCE.
items.because: It delays the development work most relevant to a frontend engineering reader.

items.says: The Barista entry takes space from development experience with routine duties.
items.because: Its two responsibility-focused bullets show no outcomes.

items.says: The drinks and stocking duties have no stated outcome.
“Prepared” is past tense in a current role.
“cafØ” contains a corrupted character instead of “café.”
items.because: The corrupted character can make the résumé look unproofread.

items.says: The opening and cash-count responsibilities have no stated outcome.
“Opened” and “handled” are past tense in a current role.
“Page performance” does not identify the measure or comparison point behind the 35% improvement.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what changed or judge the starting point.

items.says: The tests’ result is framed as an aside rather than their outcome.
Storing user input in React state does not prevent cross-site scripting when it is rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
items.because: That rendering method bypasses React’s normal text escaping, and state does not sanitize the content.

items.says: The claim that cross-site scripting was prevented has no stated verification.
items.because: A reader cannot see what supports the prevention claim.

items.says: The hotel-search bullet does not lead with its strongest results.
items.because: The load-time and bookings results follow the rebuild description, making them harder to notice.

items.says: “Owned” does not say what action was taken with the websites and library.
items.because: The reader can see the scope of responsibility but not the work performed.

items.says: The websites and library responsibility has no stated outcome.
items.because: The line shows scope without showing what the work made better.

items.says: The reduction in broken-page reports comes after the process details.
items.because: The reader must get through the interview and preview-mode description before seeing the key result.

items.says: The reduction in failed audits follows the checklist description.
items.because: The clearest evidence of impact is less immediate.

items.says: The reduction in search time comes after the rebuild and filtering details.
items.because: The reader sees the implementation before the main result.

items.says: The live-arrivals bullet does not say how live data reached the app.
items.because: The feature and its reach are clear, but the technical contribution is not.

items.says: “Against 2.9s before” makes the previous load time awkward to parse.
The comma and “and” make the agency link’s connection to open-sourcing less direct.
The booking-flow bullet names React and TypeScript, while the project heading names Vue.
items.because: A reader cannot tell which frontend stack the project used.

items.says: “Worked on” is vague, and the bullet gives no outcome of the frontend work.
items.because: It does not show the specific contribution or why it mattered.

items.says: “Using React and TypeScript” names tools without showing how they built the booking flow.
The calendar component and tests have no stated outcome.
items.because: The edge cases show scope, but not what benefit the work delivered.

items.says: The calendar-component bullet should come before the booking-flow bullet.
items.because: It is the more specific contribution and would clarify the project work sooner.

items.says: “Lifting bookings by about a tenth” does not specify a relative change or percentage-point change, or the measurement period.
items.because: A reader cannot interpret the size or period of the bookings result.

items.says: The travel-search and bookings bullet reads as unrelated to the Library Room Booking project.
items.because: Unlike the booking-flow and calendar bullets, it makes the attribution of project details questionable.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled; the tool name is “Storybook.”
items.because: The incorrect name can look like a proofreading error.

items.says: “Angular” is listed without corresponding experience or a project that plausibly used it.
items.because: A reader cannot connect the tool to described work.
